name: Counter-loop
summary: Loop your opponent's loop back from a step or two behind the table.
whenToUse: When your opponent loops and you have stepped back: instead of blocking, answer with your own topspin.

keyPoints.stance: Wide and low, right foot back (left foot if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Full turn of hips and shoulders, legs push, body rotates through the ball.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Long and mostly forward, finishing in front of the forehead.
keyPoints.timing: After the top of the bounce, as the ball starts to drop.
keyPoints.tablePosition: One to two metres from the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Wide for balance, then pulls in to speed up the turn.
keyPoints.batArm: Relaxed and long at the start; closed bat; acceleration at contact.
keyPoints.recovery: Step back into position; the rally continues at distance.
keyPoints.anticipation: Read their loop: heavy and slow means more time; fast and flat means shorter swing.

cues: Over the top of the ball

learningPath.task: Watch from the side: the swing is long and forward, and the player is far back.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.
3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Were you a step or two back?
Did the legs start the swing?
Did the bat close over the ball?

learningPath.task: Counter heavy, slow topspin from a feed.
Open with a loop against a long push, then counter-loop when your partner loops back.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent opens with a loop to your forehand and you are a step back.
gamePatterns.how: Counter-loop cross-court with spin, then step back in.

fixes: Brush over the top of the ball
Start the turn as soon as you see the loop

penholdNotes: Same body action. Keep the wrist firm; distance needs body power, not wrist.
